text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.6% today to $437.75, extending a steep two-week decline of 7.6%. The primary driver was crude oil dropping more than 7% on Monday after news broke that the U.S. and Iran are pursuing diplomatic talks, reducing concerns about Middle East conflict escalating into a sustained supply disruption. As a refiner, Marathon's profitability depends partly on the spread between crude costs and the products it sells; when oil prices fall sharply, that benefit shrinks, and investors punished the stock accordingly.

The decline also reflects caution heading into Big Oil earnings season—analysts flagged that forward guidance matters as much as reported results, and refiner stocks can face headwinds if crude remains soft or if demand signals weaken. Leadership changes and a company update announced by Marathon on October 29th added uncertainty just as the broader oil market was turning downward.
